title: Toric comparison for ideals, saturated blowups and smoothness
statement:
Let $M$ be a fine torsion-free monoscheme with a finite affine cover, let $k$ be a field, and put $X=k[M]$ [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. On each connected component use its torus $T$. Then:

(i) The map $I\mapsto k[I]$ is a bijection between coherent monoid ideals of $M$ and coherent $T$-equivariant ring ideals of $X$, allowing the empty monoid ideal to correspond to the zero ring ideal. It commutes with localization and pullback along monoscheme morphisms. The ideal $k[I]$ is the whole structure sheaf exactly when $I=\mathcal M$, and it is nonzero on a connected component exactly when $I$ is nonempty there.

(ii) For a coherent monoid ideal $I$ nonempty on every component, there is a canonical torus-equivariant identification $\operatorname{Bl}_{k[I]}(k[M])^\nu\simeq k[\operatorname{Bl}_I(M)^{\rm sat}]$, with the original dense torus unchanged. The saturated monoscheme blowup is again fine, torsion free and admits a finite affine cover. The identification respects localization and smooth pullback.

(iii) A smooth morphism $N\to M$ of fine monoschemes induces a smooth morphism $k[N]\to k[M]$ of schemes. If $k[M]\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth, then $M$ is smooth. In particular, if $k=\mathbf Q$ and $\mathbf Q[M]$ is regular, then every stalk of $M$ is $\mathbf N^r\oplus\mathbf Z^t$ for finite $r,t\ge0$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.17--3.1.23, Lemmas 3.2.9, 3.2.12 and 3.2.15, Lemma 3.2.17 and Corollary 3.2.18, printed pp.101--105; regular-over-Q application in 3.2.19, p.106. No Stacks tag states this monoidal-geometric result.

proof.text: We work on affine monoid charts $\operatorname{Spec}_{\rm mon}P$ using [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. The ring $k[P]$ has the specified monomial basis. Localization at $a\in P$ sends $e^p$ to the same symbol and identifies $k[P]_{e^a}$ with $k[P[a^{-1}]]$: its inverse sends $e^{p-na}$ to $e^p/(e^a)^n$. The two assignments respect the defining equality in the monoid localization. They also identify the ideal extended from $I$ with $k[I+\mathbf N(-a)]$. We will glue these explicit monomial identifications on overlaps; all maps send each monomial to the monomial with its image exponent.

source.place: Expose VIII, Proposition 3.2.2 proof and 3.2.14, printed pp.103,105; explicit localization calculation.

proof.text: On a connected component let $L$ be its generic group and put $A=k[P]$, $B=A\otimes_k k[L]$. By [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization], equivariance of $J$ says $JB=\mu(J)B$, where $\mu(e^p)=e^p\otimes e^p$. Thus for $f=\sum_p c_pe^p\in J$, $\mu(f)\in J\otimes_k k[L]$. Apply the coefficient functional at $e^p$ on the second tensor factor: $c_pe^p\in J$, and hence $e^p\in J$ whenever $c_p\ne0$, since $k$ is a field. Set $I=\{p\in P:e^p\in J\}$. Multiplication by $e^q$ shows $I+P\subseteq I$, and the coefficient calculation gives $J=\bigoplus_{p\in I}ke^p=k[I]$. Conversely, for $J=k[I]$, $\mu(e^p)=(e^p\otimes1)(1\otimes e^p)$ and $e^p\otimes1=\mu(e^p)(1\otimes e^{-p})$; these equations give $\mu(J)B=JB$. This proves both equivariance and the inverse formula, including $I=\varnothing$, $J=0$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.2.14 and proof of Lemma 3.2.15, printed p.105; coefficient extraction written explicitly.

proof.text: Coherence in this bijection is also local. If $I$ has finite generators, the corresponding monomials generate $k[I]$. Conversely choose finite ring generators of a coherent $J$ on an affine chart, and collect their finitely many support exponents. Step 2 puts every corresponding monomial in $J$; these monomials generate $J$, since they contain the chosen generators and lie in $J$. Their exponents generate $I$: expanding products in a monomial generating set shows that a monomial in the generated ring ideal has exponent equal to a generator plus an element of $P$. The inverse formula and Step 1 therefore glue uniquely on overlaps. For a monoid map $P\to Q$, extending the ideal on either side gives the monomials with exponents in the ideal generated by its image, which proves pullback compatibility. The basis shows $k[I]=k[P]$ exactly when $0\in I$, equivalently $I=P$, and $k[I]\ne0$ exactly when $I\ne\varnothing$. Check these assertions on the affine charts of each component. This finishes (i).

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.18 and 3.2.14--3.2.15, printed pp.101,105; finite-support and pullback details.

proof.text: For (ii), choose finite generators $a_1,\ldots,a_s$ of $I$ on an affine chart. Here $s>0$: nonemptiness on a component persists to every nonempty monoid chart since localization cannot turn a nonempty monoid ideal into the empty set. Put $J=k[I]$. By [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover], the ordinary blowup is covered by the charts $\operatorname{Spec}k[P][J/e^{a_i}]$. In its fraction field this chart ring is precisely $k[C_i]$, where $C_i=P[I-a_i]\subset P^{\rm gp}$: the generators $e^p$ and $e^{b-a_i}$ are exactly the generators on both sides. This is also the ordinary monoscheme blowup chart in [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. On the overlap of charts $a_i,a_j$, both identifications invert $e^{a_j-a_i}$, respectively its inverse on the other chart, so they agree on every monomial. Together with Step 1 this gives the canonical ordinary toric blowup comparison on all of $M$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.19 and Lemma 3.2.17 proof, printed pp.101,105.

proof.text: Each $C_i$ is finitely generated, integral and has group completion $P^{\rm gp}$, since it contains $P$ and is contained in that group. Apply [lem-trf-affine-monoid-algebra-normalization] to $C_i$: the normalized chart is $\operatorname{Spec}k[C_i^{\rm sat}]$. These are exactly the saturated monoid blowup charts. By [lem-trf-fine-monoid-finite-saturation], saturation commutes with their monoid localizations, so the monomial identifications from Step 4 agree on the normalized overlaps as well. They glue to the identification in (ii). Finite generation of every $C_i^{\rm sat}$ follows from that same node; integrality and the unchanged torsion-free group completion give fineness and torsion-freeness. There are finitely many such charts on a finite affine cover of $M$. Inverting all monomials gives $k[P^{\rm gp}]$ on each side, and all comparison maps act identically there. Thus the original dense torus is unchanged, and the comparison is torus equivariant. The same chart calculation after any monoid localization proves localization compatibility.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.2.9, Corollary 3.2.18 and 3.1.17--3.1.20, printed pp.101,104--105.

proof.text:
For smooth morphisms use smallest affine neighborhoods, so a stalk splitting is an actual local chart splitting. Indeed, in $\operatorname{Spec}_{\rm mon}P$ at a prime $\mathfrak p$, its complementary face is generated by those members of a finite generating set of $P$ lying outside $\mathfrak p$. If $a$ is their sum (or $0$ for an empty set), then $D(a)$ is contained in every neighborhood of $\mathfrak p$ and its section monoid is the stalk $P_{\mathfrak p}$. This gives a smallest affine neighborhood at each point, also in a general fine monoscheme. A morphism maps the smallest neighborhood of a point into the smallest neighborhood of its image, and its map of sections is its stalk map. Consequently a smooth monoscheme morphism has on these neighborhoods the chart $P\to P\oplus\mathbf N^r\oplus\mathbf Z^t$ of [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. Its realized ring map is
$$k[P]\longrightarrow k[P][x_1,\ldots,x_r,y_1^{\pm1},\ldots,y_t^{\pm1}].$$
This map is smooth by the definition [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]: it has the finite presentation with inverse variables $v_j$ and relations $y_jv_j-1$; across a square-zero thickening lift the $x_i$ arbitrarily and lift each $y_j$ as a unit, whose inverse then supplies $v_j$. A lift of a unit is a unit because $1+n$ has inverse $1-n$ when $n^2=0$. These local morphisms cover the source realization, so [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source] proves that $k[N]\to k[M]$ is smooth. This proves the first assertion of (iii).

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.4(iii), 3.1.15--3.1.16 and Lemma 3.2.12(i), printed pp.98,100,104; local Laurent-polynomial lifting argument expanded.

proof.text:
We can now check smooth pullback in (ii) on the same smallest neighborhoods. In a chart $Q=P\oplus H$, $H=\mathbf N^r\oplus\mathbf Z^t$, the extended ideal is $I+H$. Its chart at $(a,0)$ is
$$Q[(I+H)-(a,0)]=P[I-a]\oplus H.$$
Saturation of this chart is $P[I-a]^{\rm sat}\oplus H$: if a positive multiple of $(g,h)$ lies in the product, saturation of $H$ gives $h\in H$, and the first coordinate gives $g\in P[I-a]^{\rm sat}$; conversely take a multiple witnessing the first coordinate. Thus the realized saturated chart is obtained from $k[P[I-a]^{\rm sat}]$ by the same polynomial and invertible variables. The normalized scheme chart is the very same algebra by [lem-trf-affine-monoid-algebra-normalization]. The base changes and comparison maps send $e^p,x_i,y_j$ to themselves; hence the chart squares commute and so do their localizations and gluings. This is the asserted smooth-pullback compatibility, including identities and composites, since substitution on these generators composes. No general assertion about normalization under arbitrary base change is needed.

source.place: Expose VIII, Remark 3.1.23 and Lemma 3.2.17/Corollary 3.2.18, printed pp.101,105; smooth product-chart calculation.

proof.text: For the converse smoothness assertion, restrict to any affine monoid chart $P$ of $M$. Smoothness restricts to its open realization by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source]. By [lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal], $\operatorname{Spec}k[P]$ is regular and all its local rings are normal domains. By [lem-trf-affine-monoid-algebra-normalization], $k[P^{\rm sat}]$ is finite over $k[P]$ and has the same fraction field. The induced finite birational map of integral schemes is therefore an isomorphism by [lem-trf-finite-birational-normal-iso]. The inclusion $k[P]\subseteq k[P^{\rm sat}]$ is consequently surjective; comparing monomial bases yields $P=P^{\rm sat}$. We have reduced to a fine saturated torsion-free $P$, with $k[P]$ smooth and regular.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.2.12(ii) proof, printed p.104, reduction to saturation using normality and the finite toric normalization.

proof.text: Let $U=P^\times$ and $R=P/U$. Apply [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening] with the face $F=U$ (localizing at units does not change $P$). It says $R$ is fine saturated sharp and $R^{\rm gp}=P^{\rm gp}/U$ is finite free. The group $U$ is finitely generated: a unit expressed as a sum of monoid generators uses only unit generators, because every summand of a unit is a unit. It is torsion free as a subgroup of $P^{\rm gp}$, so [lem-trf-fg-torsionfree-group-free] gives $U\cong\mathbf Z^t$. Lift a basis of $R^{\rm gp}$ to $P^{\rm gp}$ and extend by integer linearity to a section $s$ of $P^{\rm gp}\to R^{\rm gp}$. For $q\in R$ choose $p\in P$ above it. Then $p-s(q)\in U$, so $s(q)\in P$ since units can be subtracted. Hence $U\oplus R\to P$, $(u,q)\mapsto u+s(q)$, is a monoid isomorphism, by existence and uniqueness of the two group coordinates. Write $r=\operatorname{rank}R^{\rm gp}$.

source.place: Expose VIII, proof of Lemma 3.2.12(ii), printed p.104, splitting the unit group; Expose VI 3.7(a) for finite free sharp group completions.

proof.text: Let $A$ be the set of atoms of the sharp monoid $R$, namely the nonzero elements not expressible as a sum of two nonzero elements. It is finite and generates $R$. To see this without an infinite descent, choose an inclusion-minimal finite generating set of nonzero elements. If a generator $b$ decomposes, expand its two summands in these generators. An occurrence of $b$ in the expansion would cancel to give a sum of nonzero elements equal to $0$, impossible in a sharp integral monoid, unless one summand were $0$. Thus the expansion omits $b$, contradicting minimality. All generators are therefore atoms; conversely an atom must be one of them, since an expression of length at least two decomposes it. This proves the claim, including $R=\{0\}$ and $A=\varnothing$.

source.place: Expose VIII, proof of Lemma 3.2.12(ii), printed pp.104--105, assertion that the indecomposable nonunits generate; finite minimal-generators argument written out.

proof.text:
Using $P\cong R\oplus\mathbf Z^t$, put $B=k[P]=k[R][y_1^{\pm1},\ldots,y_t^{\pm1}]$ and let $\mathfrak m$ be the maximal ideal generated by $e^q$ for $q\ne0$ in $R$ and by $y_j-1$. Its residue field is $k$. Modulo $\mathfrak m^2$, the classes of $e^a$ for $a\in A$ and $y_j-1$ span: decomposable exponents give products of two nonunits, and $y^n\equiv1+\sum_j n_j(y_j-1)$ modulo the square, also for negative $n_j$. They are independent. Indeed map $B$ to the square-zero algebra $k\oplus\bigoplus_{a\in A}k\epsilon_a\oplus\bigoplus_{j=1}^t k\delta_j$ by
$$e^{(q,n)}\longmapsto\begin{cases}1+\sum_jn_j\delta_j&q=0,\\ \epsilon_q&q\in A,\\0&q\ne0\text{ decomposable}.\end{cases}$$
The rule is multiplicative: a sum of two nonzero exponents is decomposable, and multiplication by a unit does not change the first-order atom term. It sends the displayed classes to the distinct basis vectors. Localization at $\mathfrak m$ does not change this quotient, since $B/\mathfrak m=k$ and every denominator acts there by a nonzero scalar. Thus the local cotangent space of $B_{\mathfrak m}$ has dimension $|A|+t$.

source.place: Expose VIII, proof of Lemma 3.2.12(ii), printed pp.104--105; monomial cotangent computation with unit variables retained, and explicit first-order independence test.

proof.text: The finite torsion-free group $P^{\rm gp}$ has a basis by [lem-trf-fg-torsionfree-group-free], of size $r+t$ by Step 9. Its group algebra is a Laurent polynomial algebra in that many variables. Inverting all monomials identifies the fraction field of $B=k[P]$ with the rational function field in those variables: monomials with distinct lattice exponents are linearly independent, and the basis of the group generates all fractions. Its transcendence degree over $k$ is $r+t$. The algebra $B$ is finite type, generated by the monomials of a finite generating set of $P$, and it is a domain by [lem-trf-affine-monoid-algebra-normalization]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-trdeg] gives $\dim B_{\mathfrak m}=r+t$. This local ring is regular by Step 8, so [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension] and Step 11 give $|A|+t=r+t$, hence $|A|=r$. The atoms generate $R$ by Step 10 and hence generate the free group $R^{\rm gp}$. A generating $r$-tuple in a rank-$r$ free abelian group is a basis (its surjective integer matrix has an integer right inverse, so determinant is a unit). Therefore the surjection $\mathbf N^A\to R$ is injective, as any equality would be an integer relation in that basis. It follows that $P\cong\mathbf N^r\oplus\mathbf Z^t$. Applying this to the smallest affine neighborhood of each point proves $M$ smooth.

source.place: Expose VIII, proof of Lemma 3.2.12(ii), printed pp.104--105, equality of dimension and cotangent dimension and independence of the atom generators.

proof.text: Finally $\mathbf Q[M]\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q$ is locally of finite type: on any affine chart, the monomials of finitely many monoid generators generate its coordinate algebra. The field $\mathbf Q$ is perfect (every characteristic-zero field extension is separable). If $\mathbf Q[M]$ is regular, [lem-trf-regular-perfect-field-smooth] makes this morphism smooth. Steps 8--12 then give the required form $\mathbf N^r\oplus\mathbf Z^t$ for every stalk. All arguments are local and include the empty monoscheme, the empty ideal in (i), the unit ideal in (ii), the zero monoid and arbitrary finite torus factors. This finishes (iii) and the item.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.2.19, printed p.106, regular characteristic-zero terminal toric schemes; smoothness reflection from Lemma 3.2.12(ii).

proof_origin.place: Expose VIII 3.1.17--3.1.23, Lemmas 3.2.9, 3.2.12, 3.2.15, 3.2.17 and Corollary 3.2.18, printed pp.101--105, and 3.2.19 p.106; coefficient, finite-generator, product-chart and cotangent details expanded explicitly.

lean.statement: theorem toric_ideal_comparison (k : Type u) [Field k] (M : Fine.{u}) (hM : M.IsTorsionFree) : (∀ I : IdealFamily M, IsCoherentIdeal I → (∀ U : (realization k M).affineOpens, ((ringIdeal k I).ideal U).FG) ∧ IsTorusEquivariant k M (ringIdeal k I)) ∧ (∀ J : (realization k M).IdealSheafData, (∀ U : (realization k M).affineOpens, (J.ideal U).FG) → IsTorusEquivariant k M J → ∃! I : IdealFamily M, IsCoherentIdeal I ∧ ringIdeal k I = J) ∧ (∀ (I I' : IdealFamily M), IsCoherentIdeal I → IsCoherentIdeal I' → ringIdeal k I = ringIdeal k I' → I = I') ∧ ringIdeal k (emptyIdeal M) = ⊥ ∧ (∀ I : IdealFamily M, IsCoherentIdeal I → (ringIdeal k I = ⊤ ↔ I = wholeIdeal M) ∧ ∀ C : ToricComponent M, (ringIdeal k I).comap (componentι k C) ≠ ⊥ ↔ ∃ x : M.space, ConnectedComponents.mk x = C.component ∧ (idealStalk I x).Nonempty) ∧ (∀ (N : Fine.{u}) (f : Hom N M) (I : IdealFamily M), IsCoherentIdeal I → IsCoherentIdeal (pullbackIdeal f I) ∧ ringIdeal k (pullbackIdeal f I) = (ringIdeal k I).comap (realizationMap k f))
